notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only via round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0006] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Money-moving functions take keyword-only idempotency_key: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Check it first via ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing entry with that key and return the original result without reapplying; include idempotency_key in the audit.record() call.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0007] Raise BillingError with code and message: For domain validation failures in billing code, raise `BillingError(code, message)` from `ledgerly.errors` rather than `ValueError`.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
